summary: A humorous neighborhood feature on how Maplewood Heights has become saturated with technology after September 2023, from drone mail delivery and smart mailboxes to robotic gardeners, surveillance orbs, smart fridges, emoji-based conversation, VR block parties and fitness gadgets. Residents are split between delight and dismay, with quotes from locals like Margaret Smith, Carl Jenkins and Tina Gonzalez. Mrs. Henderson and her typewriter are presented as the last analogue holdout.
one_line: A satirical look at how drones, smart homes, surveillance orbs and VR have transformed the suburb of Maplewood Heights, with locals split on the change.
key_facts: Mail carrier Jim O'Hara has been replaced in Maplewood Heights by the drone delivery service "AirSnail".
Mailboxes are now 'smart', with sensors that notify homeowners when mail arrives or when anyone gets too close.
Margaret Smith, a retiree from Maple Street, joked that "at least someone's paying attention to me in my old age, even if it's just a box of bolts."
RoboGardenerX2000 is a device that zaps weeds, trims lawns and sprays roses with plant dye.
Carl Jenkins, once known for his prize petunias, now uses a touchpad app that knows the forecast before the news does.
AI-powered hovering cameras called "Sentinels" record and warn jaywalkers at street corners.
Privacy advocate Jane Doe (not her real name) campaigns against excessive monitoring and jokes about chips in brains to curb "jaythinking".

In the Great Vegan Cheese Incident of November 2023, George Bentley's smart fridge insisted on plant-based alternatives, and his golden retriever Buddy renounced humankind in favor of cheddar-scented humans.
Tina Gonzalez, a local coffee shop owner, says customers send a 'coffee cup' emoji to her automated beverage dispenser to order.
Residents use emoji flags to signal social readiness: green for 'chat welcome,' yellow for 'smile and nod only,' and red for 'I haven’t had my coffee, back off.'
Virtual block parties in VR headsets have become the new "hangouts", with no cleanup but a risk of feeling lonelier among avatars.
Gary "Lawnmower Man" Thompson wears a VR helmet that makes mowing look like a battle against a pixelated horde.
Mrs. Henderson is the last analogue holdout and hands visitors freshly typed notes about the weather from her typewriter.
